Library borrowers can keep books for two weeks.
The borrower promised to be careful.

easy.def: The person in charge at work.
examples: Mom's boss is kind.
The boss gave us jobs.
Who is the boss here?

more.def: A person who is in charge of other workers.
examples: The boss thanked the workers for finishing early.
My dad asked his boss for a day off.
The bakery's boss starts work before dawn.

easy.def: Always telling others what to do.
examples: She is bossy.
Don't be bossy.
A bossy kid.

more.def: Fond of telling other people what to do in a rude or too forceful way.
examples: My older sister is bossy and tells me where to sit.
Don't be bossy; let everyone have a turn to choose.
The bossy parrot squawked orders at everyone.

easy.def: Having to do with plants.
examples: We visited a botanical garden.
The botanical book has flowers.
A botanical drawing.

more.def: Having to do with plants and the study of plants.
examples: We visited the botanical garden to see rare flowers.
The artist made a botanical drawing of a leaf.
A botanical expert explained how ferns grow.

easy.def: A scientist who studies plants.
examples: The botanist studied flowers.
A botanist loves plants.
The botanist took notes.

more.def: A scientist who studies plants.
examples: The botanist studied flowers in the rain forest.
A botanist can tell you the name of any tree.
The botanist discovered a new kind of orchid.

easy.def: The study of plants.
examples: She studies botany.
Botany is about plants.
He likes botany.

more.def: The scientific study of plants.
examples: She studies botany at school.
Botany teaches how plants grow.
He took a class in botany.

easy.def: To do badly.
examples: He botched the job.
She botched the cake.
They botched it.

more.def: To do something badly by making mistakes.
examples: He botched the repair and made it worse.
She botched the recipe.
They botched the plan.

easy.def: The two of them.
examples: I like both.
Both are good.
Hold it with both hands.

more.def: The one and the other of two people or things.
examples: Both of my brothers play the guitar.
I tried the red and the blue shirts, and I like both.
Both teams ran onto the field at the same time.

easy.def: To make someone upset by interrupting.
examples: Do not bother the baby.
The noise bothers me.
Flies bother the horse.

more.def: To annoy someone or interrupt them, or to cause worry.
examples: The loud music bothered the neighbors.
Please do not bother me while I read.
Does the cold bother you?

easy.def: Annoying.
examples: The fly was bothersome.
A bothersome noise.
The bothersome mosquito.

more.def: Annoying and a little troublesome.
examples: The buzzing fly was bothersome.
The bothersome noise kept me awake.
It was a bothersome little cough.

easy.def: A container for drinks with a narrow top.
examples: A bottle of milk.
Water in a bottle.
The baby drinks from a bottle.

more.def: A container, usually of glass or plastic, with a narrow neck for holding liquids.
examples: She filled the bottle with water.
He put a message in a bottle.
The baby drinks milk from a bottle.

easy.def: Putting drink into bottles.
examples: The bottling is done.
Bottling takes time.
The bottling plant is busy.

more.def: The act of putting liquid into bottles.
examples: The bottling of the juice took all day.
The factory has a machine for bottling.
Workers checked each bottle during bottling.

easy.def: The lowest part of something.
examples: The toy is at the bottom of the box.
Sink to the bottom.
Sign your name at the bottom.

more.def: The lowest part of something, farthest from the top.
examples: A coin lay at the bottom of the pool.
The answer is at the bottom of the page.
We waited at the bottom of the stairs.

easy.def: Lowest.
examples: The bottom shelf is full of toys.
Look at the bottom drawer.
He is in the bottom bunk.

more.def: Placed at the lowest point.
examples: Put the heavy books on the bottom shelf.
The bottom bunk is easier for little kids.
The cat sleeps in the bottom drawer.

easy.def: With no end at the bottom.
examples: The pit looked bottomless.
A bottomless well.
The lake seemed bottomless.

more.def: Seeming to have no bottom, or never running out.
examples: The well looked bottomless in the dark.
He has a bottomless appetite and eats all day.
The bottomless bowl of soup never ran out.

easy.def: A big branch of a tree.
examples: The bird sat on the bough.
A bough bent down.
The bough broke.

more.def: A large branch of a tree.
examples: A thick bough hung over the pond.
The bird built its nest on a high bough.
Apples hung heavily from the bough.

easy.def: A very big rock.
examples: A boulder blocked the path.
I sat on a boulder.
The boulder was big.

more.def: A very large rock that is too heavy to lift.
examples: A giant boulder rolled down the hill and stopped in the stream.
The hikers climbed over a huge boulder.
Moss grew on the side of the boulder.

easy.def: A wide street with trees.
examples: We drove down the boulevard.
The boulevard is wide.
Trees line the boulevard.

more.def: A broad street, often with trees along both sides.
examples: The parade went down the main boulevard.
Tall palm trees lined the boulevard.
We strolled along the boulevard to the park.

easy.def: To spring back after hitting something.
examples: The ball will bounce.
I bounce the ball.
The ball bounced off the wall.

more.def: To spring back quickly after hitting something.
examples: The ball bounced twice before she caught it.
She bounced the ball on the floor.
The kids bounced on the trampoline.

easy.def: A spring back after hitting something.
examples: The ball took a high bounce.
I heard a bounce.
The bounce was high.

more.def: The act of springing back after hitting something.
examples: The bounce of the basketball echoed through the gym.
The bounce of the rubber ball surprised us.
A high bounce sent it over the fence.

easy.def: Full of bounce.
examples: A bouncy ball.
The bed is bouncy.
The puppy is bouncy.

more.def: Full of bounce, so that it springs back or moves in a lively way.
examples: A bouncy ball sprang high off the pavement.
The bouncy castle was a hit at the party.
The puppy was so bouncy that it leaped all around the yard.

easy.def: Sure to happen.
examples: She is bound to win.
It is bound to rain.
The ice is bound to melt.

more.def: Certain or sure to do something.
examples: The team is bound to win after all that practice.
It is bound to rain with those dark clouds.
He is bound to be late again.

easy.def: To jump with long steps.
examples: The deer bounded across the field.
The puppy bounded up the stairs.
She bounded down the hall.

more.def: To leap or run with long, springy steps.
examples: The deer bounded across the meadow.
The puppy bounded up the steps to greet us.
She bounded out of bed on the first day of vacation.

easy.def: A line that shows where a place ends.
examples: The fence is the boundary of our yard.
The white line is the boundary of the field.
A wall marks the boundary of the farm.

more.def: A line or edge that marks where one area ends and another begins.
examples: The river forms the boundary between the two countries.
The ball rolled past the boundary, so play stopped.
Mountains form a natural boundary between the two valleys.

easy.def: With plenty.
examples: A bountiful harvest.
The tree gave bountiful fruit.
A bountiful meal.

more.def: Giving or having plenty, in a generous way.
examples: The farmers had a bountiful harvest.
The tree was bountiful with apples.
We enjoyed a bountiful meal at Grandma's.

easy.def: A reward for catching something.
examples: A bounty was offered.
The bounty was one hundred dollars.
They offered a bounty.

more.def: A reward that is offered for finding or catching something or someone.
examples: A bounty was offered for the lost dog.
The town offered a bounty for the rats.
A large bounty was offered for the missing treasure.

easy.def: A large amount of something good.
examples: The garden gave a bounty of tomatoes.
The farm's bounty was great.
A bounty of fruit.

more.def: A rich supply of something good.
examples: The garden gave us a bounty of tomatoes.
The harvest was a bounty.
The orchard offered a bounty of apples.

easy.def: A bunch of flowers.
examples: She got a bouquet.
The bouquet is pretty.
I picked a bouquet.

more.def: A bunch of flowers that are tied together to be given or carried.
examples: She carried a bouquet of roses down the aisle.
I picked a bouquet of wild flowers for my mom.
A bouquet of tulips sat on the kitchen table.

easy.def: A short time of being sick or busy.
examples: I had a bout of the flu.
She had a bout of hiccups.
He had a short bout of work.

more.def: A short period when something happens, such as an illness or a burst of activity.
examples: She had a bout of the flu in the winter.
After a bout of hiccups, he drank some water.
The two boxers had a three-round bout.

easy.def: A small shop that sells nice clothes or gifts.
examples: Mom shops at a boutique.
The boutique sells hats.
We went to a boutique.

more.def: A small shop that sells fashionable clothes, gifts or other special things.
examples: Mom bought a scarf at the little boutique.
The boutique sold hats and handmade jewelry.
We found a birthday gift in a boutique downtown.

easy.def: To bend forward to show thanks or respect.
examples: The actors bow.
I bowed to the teacher.
The dancers bowed.

more.def: To bend your body forward at the waist to show respect or to thank an audience.
examples: The actors bowed at the end of the play.
The knights bowed to the queen.
She bowed her head in thanks.

easy.def: A ribbon tied in a pretty way.
examples: She tied a bow in her hair.
The gift has a red bow.
The ribbon makes a bow.

more.def: A knot made with loops, used to tie ribbons and shoelaces.
examples: He tied his shoes with a neat bow.
A big red bow decorated the gift.
She wore a bow in her hair.

easy.def: A shady spot under trees or vines.
examples: We sat in the bower.
The bower was cool.
A bower of leaves.

more.def: A shady spot made by the branches of trees or climbing plants.
examples: We sat in a cool bower of vines.
A bower of roses shaded the garden bench.
Birds built nests in the leafy bower.

easy.def: A deep, round dish for food.
examples: I eat soup from a bowl.
The bowl is full of fruit.
The dog has a water bowl.

more.def: A deep, round dish used for holding food or liquid.
examples: She poured cereal into a bowl.
A bowl of apples sat on the table.
The puppy drank from its bowl.

easy.def: A person who rolls the ball in bowling, or a round hat.
examples: The bowler rolled the ball.
A bowler hat.
The bowler got a strike.

more.def: A person who plays bowling, or the player in cricket who throws the ball; also a round hat with a small brim.
examples: The bowler rolled the ball down the lane and knocked down every pin.
In cricket, the bowler throws the ball to the batter.
He wore a black bowler hat.

easy.def: A game where you roll a ball to knock down pins.
examples: I like bowling.
We went bowling.
Bowling is fun.

more.def: A game in which you roll a heavy ball down a lane to knock over pins.
examples: We went bowling on Friday night.
Bowling shoes are rented at the alley.
She scored a strike in bowling.

easy.def: The string of a bow.
examples: She pulled the bowstring.
The bowstring is tight.
A bowstring snapped.

more.def: The tight string of a bow that you pull back to shoot an arrow.
examples: The archer pulled the bowstring back.
The bowstring twanged when she let go.
A bowstring is made of strong cord.

easy.def: A container with straight sides.
examples: Put the toys in the box.
The box is big.
She opened the box.

more.def: A container with flat sides and often a lid, used to hold things.
examples: He packed his books in a cardboard box.
A box of crayons sat on the desk.
The cat curled up in an empty box.

easy.def: A train car shaped like a box.
examples: The boxcar is on the train.
A boxcar carries goods.
A red boxcar rolled by.

more.def: A closed railroad car used for carrying goods.
examples: The train pulled a long line of boxcars.
A red boxcar carried grain to the city.
We counted the boxcars as the freight train passed.

easy.def: A person who boxes.
examples: The boxer trained hard.
A boxer wears gloves.
He is a boxer.

more.def: A person who fights in the sport of boxing.
examples: The boxer trained hard at the gym.
A boxer wears padded gloves.
The boxer won the match.

easy.def: A dog with a short, wrinkled face.
examples: A boxer is a type of dog.
The boxer wagged its tail.
We have a boxer.

more.def: A strong, muscular dog with a short coat and a flat, wrinkled face.
examples: A boxer is a friendly, playful dog.
The boxer jumped up to greet us.
Our boxer loves to play fetch.

easy.def: A sport where two people punch each other with big gloves.
examples: He likes boxing.
Boxing uses big gloves.
She watched boxing on TV.

more.def: A sport in which two fighters wearing padded gloves hit each other, following rules.
examples: He trains in boxing at the gym.
Boxing takes strength and speed.
Boxing gloves are big and padded.

easy.def: Shaped like a box.
examples: The car is boxy.
A boxy house.
The boxy shape.

more.def: Square or shaped like a box.
examples: The old car was boxy.
They lived in a boxy house.
The boxy robot rolled across the room.

easy.def: A male child.
examples: The boy is my brother.
A boy kicked the ball.
That boy is in my class.

more.def: A male child or young man.
examples: The boy on the bus gave his seat to an older lady.
A group of boys was building a sandcastle at the beach.
He was a curious boy who asked questions about everything.

easy.def: To refuse to buy or use something as a protest.
examples: They boycott the store.
The group boycotted the shop.
We boycott the game.

more.def: To refuse to buy something, use something or take part in something as a way of protesting.
examples: The neighbors decided to boycott the shop until it changed its unfair prices.
Some students boycotted the school lunch because it was bad.
The people boycotted the buses to protest the unfair rule.

easy.def: A boy who is someone's special friend.
examples: My big sister has a boyfriend.
Her boyfriend came to the party.
My cousin's boyfriend baked a cake.

more.def: A boy or man who is in a close, loving relationship with someone.
examples: My cousin brought her boyfriend to meet our family.
His boyfriend helped him carry the boxes.
Her boyfriend gave her a ride home.

easy.def: The time when someone is a boy.
examples: In his boyhood he lived on a farm.
Boyhood is fun.
He told of his boyhood.

more.def: The time of life when a person is a boy.
examples: During his boyhood he spent summers fishing at the lake.
Grandpa told us about his boyhood.
She read about his boyhood in the book.

easy.def: Like a boy.
examples: He has a boyish grin.
A boyish smile.
His boyish face.

more.def: Like a boy in looks or ways, such as being playful.
examples: He had a boyish grin that made people smile.
His boyish charm made everyone like him.
She wore a boyish haircut.

easy.def: A dark purple berry.
examples: We picked a boysenberry.
The boysenberry is purple.
Boysenberry jam is sweet.

more.def: A large, dark purple berry that is a mix of other berries.
examples: We picked boysenberries at the farm.
Boysenberry jam is sweet and tart.
The pie was filled with boysenberries.
